record.paper_title: Geometric curvature energies: facts, trends, and open problems
record.context_brief: Higher-dimensional minimizers, invariants, and elastic knots
record.original_question: For higher-dimensional geometric curvature energies, can one identify the shapes of global minimizers? In the isotopy-finiteness theorem for submanifolds with bounded integral Menger curvature, what is the optimal constant controlling the number of isotopy types under a given energy bound? Are there meaningful topological invariants or geometric quantities for higher-dimensional knots that can be controlled by higher-dimensional geometric curvature energies? Do higher-dimensional elastic knots exist, for example as minimizers of the Willmore functional in prescribed isotopy classes, and if they do, can one say anything about their shapes?

evidence.quote: Theorem 2.2.15 (Isotopy finiteness). Let E, d > 0 be given. Then there are at most K = K(E, d, k, n, p) different ambient isotopy types among all k-dimensional Lipschitz submanifolds Σ ⊂ Rn with integral Menger curvature Mp(Σ) ≤ E and diam Σ ≤ d.

Open questions 2.2.16. Is it possible to identify the shape of global minimisers of higher-dimensional geometric curvature energies? The explicit constant in Theorem 2.2.15 is far from being optimal, what is the best constant bounding the number of isotopy types under given energy values? For curves the energies could often be related to knot invariants or to quantities like the average crossing number (2.1.17) controlling knot invariants. Are there meaningful topological invariants or geometric quantities for higher-dimensional knots that could be controlled by means of higher-dimensional geometric curvature energies? Are there higher-dimensional elastic knots, for instance minimisers of the Willmore functional in arbitrary prescribed isotopy classes? And can one say anything about their shapes?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setting. For an integer $k\ge 1$, a $k$-dimensional Lipschitz submanifold $\Sigma\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ is the image of a bi-Lipschitz immersion of a $k$-dimensional manifold into $\mathbb{R}^n$. For $p>0$, the integral Menger curvature of order $p$ is
$$\mathcal{M}^{p}(\Sigma)\;=\;\int_{\Sigma}\!\!\int_{\Sigma}\!\cdots\!\int_{\Sigma}\bigl(\mathrm{Mc}(x_0,\dots,x_{k+1})\bigr)^{p}\,d\mathcal{H}^{k}(x_0)\cdots d\mathcal{H}^{k}(x_{k+1}),$$
where $\mathrm{Mc}(x_0,\dots,x_{k+1})$ denotes the inverse of the circumradius of the unique $k$-sphere (or affine $k$-plane) through the $k+2$ points. An ambient isotopy between two submanifolds of $\mathbb{R}^n$ is a continuous one-parameter family of homeomorphisms of $\mathbb{R}^n$ deforming one to the other. The Willmore functional of an immersed closed surface $\Sigma\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ is $\mathcal{W}(\Sigma)=\int_\Sigma |H|^2\,d\mathcal{H}^2$, where $H$ is the mean curvature vector.

It is known that for every $E,d>0$ there are at most finitely many ambient isotopy types $K=K(E,d,k,n,p)$ among $k$-dimensional Lipschitz submanifolds $\Sigma\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ satisfying $\mathcal{M}^p(\Sigma)\le E$ and $\mathrm{diam}\,\Sigma\le d$.

Questions.
(a) Identify the shapes of global minimizers of higher-dimensional geometric curvature energies such as $\mathcal{M}^p$ on classes of closed $k$-dimensional submanifolds of $\mathbb{R}^n$.
(b) Determine the optimal (smallest) constant $K(E,d,k,n,p)$ in the isotopy-finiteness statement above.
(c) Identify meaningful topological invariants or geometric quantities of higher-dimensional knotted submanifolds (e.g. embedded $S^k\hookrightarrow\mathbb{R}^{k+2}$) that can be controlled by higher-dimensional geometric curvature energies, in analogy with the way the average crossing number of a closed curve is controlled by curve energies.
(d) Prove or disprove the existence of higher-dimensional elastic knots: for every prescribed ambient isotopy class of embedded closed surfaces $\Sigma\subset\mathbb{R}^3$ (or in higher codimension), does the Willmore functional $\mathcal{W}$ attain its infimum within the class, and if so, what can be said about the shape of such minimizers?
artifact.status_search_result: The four sub-questions are listed as open problems in surveys on geometric curvature energies. A literature search shows ongoing activity—Willmore minimization in prescribed isoperimetric or topological classes, tangent-point and Menger curvature energies, and elastic-knot approximations—but no published resolution of the shape of higher-dimensional minimizers, the optimal isotopy-finiteness constant, knot-type invariants controlled by $\mathcal{M}^p$ in higher dimensions, or existence/shape of Willmore minimizers in arbitrary prescribed isotopy classes. The questions therefore appear to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Willmore Minimizers with Prescribed Isoperimetric Ratio
status_evidence.snippet: Studies existence of Willmore minimizers under prescribed isoperimetric constraints, not arbitrary isotopy classes.
status_evidence.claim: Existence of Willmore minimizers in arbitrary prescribed isotopy classes remains unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Stability of a simple scheme for the approximation of elastic knots
status_evidence.snippet: Numerical approximation of elastic knots; characterization in general knot classes is wide open.
status_evidence.claim: Higher-dimensional elastic knots are not characterized in the literature.

status_evidence.title: Scale-invariant tangent-point energies for knots
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work on knot energies and their minimizers, focused mainly on curves.
status_evidence.claim: Analogous results identifying minimizers of higher-dimensional Menger-type energies are not established.
